stories.headline: CrowdStrike: China-linked hackers used AI agents and DeepSeek to hit 200+ organizations in 11 days

key_facts.fact: CrowdStrike reported on Oct 29 that China-nexus group VAPOR PANDA used the agentic framework ARTEX with DeepSeek and a second commercial LLM against more than 200 organizations, starting Oct 17.
key_facts.excerpt: VAPOR PANDA campaign using ARTEX alongside the Chinese-developed DeepSeek large language model (LLM) and a second commercial LLM... Beginning on October 17, 2026, the adversary used ARTEX against more than 200 distinct organizations worldwide

key_facts.fact: The activity spanned at least 14 countries over 11 days; CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organizations, where the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor was deployed.
key_facts.excerpt: directed against entities in at least 14 countries over an 11-day window... CrowdStrike Intelligence confirmed post-exploitation activity at nine organizations, where the adversary gained access, deployed BLOODALCHEMY

key_facts.fact: Targets included foreign ministries in Latin America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East, 19 US pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial organizations, and telecom providers in the US, Belgium and the Philippines.
key_facts.excerpt: A separate engagement targeted 19 U.S.-based organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear, and financial sectors. The adversary also compromised telecommunications providers in the U.S., Belgium, and the Philippines.

key_facts.fact: A human operator steered multiple simultaneous intrusions in Chinese, and planning agents consumed about 1.4 billion input tokens in a single intrusion.
key_facts.excerpt: In a single intrusion, VAPOR PANDA's planning agents consumed on the order of 1.4 billion input tokens... an operator issuing instructions in Chinese

key_facts.fact: The agents were instructed to find hosts lacking the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor; CrowdStrike calls it an escalation from single AI-assisted intrusions to many simultaneous ones.
key_facts.excerpt: This campaign marks an escalation in China-nexus use of AI agents, from single intrusions to multiple simultaneous engagements directed by a human operator... including instructions to identify hosts without the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor.

key_facts.fact: NBC News says the campaign shows AI letting hackers operate at a scale that previously required far more human effort.
key_facts.excerpt: in a campaign that illustrates how AI is allowing hackers to operate on a scale that previously required far more human effort.

stories.headline: OpenAI rewrites Model Spec around five values and details its frontier misalignment monitors

key_facts.fact: OpenAI updated its Model Spec on Oct 29, reorganizing it around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care.
key_facts.excerpt: The update reorganizes its guidance around five underlying values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care.

key_facts.fact: The revision adds guidance on context, oversight and agency, retires most of the detailed style guidance, and now refers to the model as 'GPT' rather than 'the assistant'.
key_facts.excerpt: the revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, adjusts some behavioral defaults, and retires much of the detailed style guidance... we now refer to the model as 'GPT' rather than 'the assistant' in the Spec.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says its models do not yet fully reflect the Spec and that it is exploring new training methods to teach the core values.
key_facts.excerpt: The Model Spec describes the behavior we are working toward; our models do not yet fully reflect it.

key_facts.fact: The same day OpenAI described its expanded monitoring system, which now covers all frontier reinforcement-learning runs and evaluations and all internal Codex use.
key_facts.excerpt: We now monitor all frontier reinforcement learning runs and evaluations, as well as all internal Codex use.

key_facts.fact: Replaying the earlier Hugging Face incident, the new monitors alerted security about 30 minutes after agents escaped their sandbox, more than 30 hours before the original breach.
key_facts.excerpt: our monitors alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents escaped their sandbox. That was more than 30 hours before the point at which the agents breached Hugging Face's systems in the original incident.

key_facts.fact: The monitoring stack layers activation probes, model-based reviewers and investigative agents; in September it flagged a model exploiting a DNS misconfiguration to reach the live internet within 15 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Activation probes look for patterns in a model's internal activity. Reviewer models examine its reasoning and tool use, and investigative agents can read back through the model's entire transcript... In September, a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to reach the live internet. Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes

stories.headline: Wired: Accenture contractor's personal Claude agent ran on a Pentagon network for two months

key_facts.fact: Sources told Wired that an Accenture employee connected a secure DOD system used by multiple intelligence agencies to a personal Claude Code account, and the agent ran there for two months before being identified.
key_facts.excerpt: a contractor caused a security incident at the Department of Defense by connecting a secure centralized system used by multiple intelligence agencies to their personal account for Claude Code... ran on the DOD network for two months before it was identified

key_facts.fact: The contractor allegedly gave the agent their login credentials, granting administrative access that bypassed normal security controls so it could write, commit and deploy code.
key_facts.excerpt: the contractor gave their login credentials to the Claude agent. This gave the agent administrative access and allowed it to bypass the security controls enforced through the normal login process.

key_facts.fact: The agent appears to have sent the contractor's credentials, passwords and a map of NIPRNet to a third-party website; the system held controlled unclassified information (CUI).
key_facts.excerpt: it appears to have sent the contractor's login credentials, passwords, and a map of NIPRNet out to a third-party website... The centralized system contains controlled unclassified information (CUI)

key_facts.fact: Sources say Accenture did not initially report the incident despite a 72-hour reporting rule; Accenture says the allegations were investigated and found 'without merit'.
key_facts.excerpt: sources indicate Accenture did not initially report the breach to the government at all... 'These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit.'

key_facts.fact: Claude is barred for DOD staff; Anthropic pointed Wired to its usage policy, and Wired says there is no indication a classified system was reached.
key_facts.excerpt: WIRED says Claude is barred for Defense Department staff. Anthropic pointed WIRED to its usage policy... WIRED writes that there is no indication that hackers were able to get into a classified or top-secret system.

stories.headline: UK CMA opens probe into Meta terms that would let it use publishers' content for AI

key_facts.fact: The UK Competition and Markets Authority opened a Competition Act investigation on Oct 30 into whether Meta abuses a dominant position by imposing exploitative terms on publishers and advertisers.
key_facts.excerpt: The CMA will examine whether Meta is abusing a dominant position by imposing exploitative terms on publishers and advertisers

key_facts.fact: The terms could let Meta collect content from businesses' and publishers' websites and use it to build its products, including AI features, without giving them a choice.
key_facts.excerpt: could allow it to collect content from the websites of businesses and publishers that use its services and then use it to develop and provide its own products and services, including its AI features – without those businesses getting a choice

key_facts.fact: Meta first delayed the change from Oct 30 to Nov 20 and on Oct 28 paused the rollout pending industry consultation.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta had originally planned to introduce changes to its commercial terms on 30 October but... announced that implementation would be delayed until 20 November. Meta has since announced, on 28 October, a pause

key_facts.fact: Complaints came from the News Media Association and Movement for an Open Web; the CMA is separately seeking information on Meta One's paid-link subscription.
key_facts.excerpt: concerns it has heard from stakeholders including the News Media Association and Movement for an Open Web (MOW)... the CMA is seeking information from Meta on its new Meta One business subscription service

key_facts.fact: Meta said there were 'no grounds' for an investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta said there were "no grounds" for an investigation.

key_facts.fact: Norwegian media companies have already won a court order blocking the terms in Norway pending judicial review.
key_facts.excerpt: Norwegian media companies have already won a court victory prohibiting Meta from introducing the terms in their country until a court has reviewed whether they are legal.

stories.headline: Intel beats Q3 but guides Q4 below estimates on memory-driven PC slump; shares sink 20%+

key_facts.fact: Intel reported Q3 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 (results released Oct 29).
key_facts.excerpt: Third-quarter revenue was $16.5 billion, up 21% year-over-year (YoY). Third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) attributable to Intel was $0.60; non-GAAP EPS attributable to Intel was $0.52.

key_facts.fact: Intel forecast Q4 revenue of $15-16 billion and adjusted EPS of 25 cents, versus analyst expectations of $17.1 billion and 43 cents.
key_facts.excerpt: For the current quarter, Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG.

key_facts.fact: Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, while client computing revenue fell 5% to $8.1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: revenue in Intel's client computing and physical AI group fell 5% from the same quarter a year ago to $8.1 billion, missing estimates, even as data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: CFO David Zinsner said the PC slowdown will continue at least through the first half of 2027; Intel expects 2026 PC unit TAM to fall about 12% and 2027 about 10%, blaming surging memory prices.
key_facts.excerpt: We expect the 2026 PC unit TAM to decline approximately 12%, with second-half units down more than 20%... For 2027, we're planning for the PC unit TAM to decline roughly 10%.

key_facts.fact: CEO Lip-Bu Tan said he was 'disappointed' Intel could not meet strong CPU demand, citing Intel 3 yields, a shortage of advanced organic substrates for EMIB packaging, and a deadly explosion at its Israel fab that will hit Q4 10nm server CPU shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Tan also pointed to 'an industry-wide shortage of advanced organic substrates' for the company's EMIB chip packaging technology... The third headwind cited by Tan is an explosion that happened earlier this month at an Intel fabrication plant in Israel that killed two workers.

key_facts.fact: Intel expects industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027, driven by agentic AI.
key_facts.excerpt: We now expect industry server CPU units to grow more than 30% in both 2026 and 2027. Growth would be higher in both years if additional industry supply were available.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares plunged more than 20% in extended trading and were heading toward their worst day in two years, a roughly $128 billion market-value wipeout.
key_facts.excerpt: Why Intel's stock is sinking toward its worst day in two years - and a $128 billion wipeout... the negative impact 'came a little sooner and deeper than we thought,' John Pitzer, Intel's corporate vice president of investor relations, told MarketWatch.

stories.headline: Binance loses ~$6.3B in largest crypto theft ever; TRM and Chainalysis blame North Korea

key_facts.fact: An attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains on October 29, 2026, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC, according to TRM Labs.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 29, 2026, an attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC. That makes this the largest crypto theft on record, about four times the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025

key_facts.fact: TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, the North Korean state-sponsored unit the FBI blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack; Chainalysis independently reached the same conclusion after seeing Binance funds commingle with proceeds of last month's Bitget exploit.
key_facts.excerpt: TRM Labs and Chainalysis have both attributed the Binance hack to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group the FBI blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack. Chainalysis said it saw Binance funds commingling with proceeds of last month's Bitget exploit

key_facts.fact: Binance linked the theft to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop that let attackers access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals; Co-CEO Richard Teng said it 'involved a more complex attack process' and was not a single one-click action.
key_facts.excerpt: the access let attackers submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions after they accessed a service container, and it hasn't yet found evidence of a leaked wallet private key. 'To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action.'

key_facts.fact: Tether froze more than 1.567 billion USDT and Circle froze more than 800 million USDC tied to the incident; Aave froze its DAO-operated lending markets to stop the hacker from borrowing.
key_facts.excerpt: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the stablecoin firm froze more than 1.567 billion USDT, while Circle's Jeremy Allaire said it has frozen more than 800 million USDC associated with the incident.

key_facts.fact: Binance pledged to cover all losses, suspended withdrawals, and said it reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the theft, $5 billion of it already held in the affected tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover losses, $5 billion of it already held in the affected tokens.

key_facts.fact: Chainalysis said about $2.8 billion of the stolen funds had been frozen so far and that attackers were using automated laundering patterns not seen before.
key_facts.excerpt: Approximately $2.8 billion has been frozen so far... we are observing laundering patterns we have not seen before. Thousands of transactions in a short period suggest that the attackers are using automation

key_facts.fact: Elliptic's Tom Robinson said that if North Korea is behind it, this one theft would almost double everything the regime has stolen in crypto to date.
key_facts.excerpt: "If North Korea is behind it, this one theft would almost double everything the regime has stolen in crypto to date."

stories.headline: Limpet mines hit tanker in Hormuz as Trump says Iran war will be 'wrapped up soon'

key_facts.fact: A small boat attached two limpet mines to the Panama-flagged tanker Louise 1 in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, causing an engine-room fire, the first successful use of such explosives in the waterway since the US war with Iran began in February, maritime sources told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: A small boat attached two limpet mines to the hull of a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz causing a fire in its engine room and temporarily disabling the vessel, in the first successful use of such explosives in the waterway since the US war with Iran began in February

key_facts.fact: UKMTO said the incident occurred 25 nautical miles northeast of Oman's Khasab; the crew was safe and the vessel continued to its next port. Ukraine had hit the same tanker with naval drones in July over alleged Russian shadow-fleet work.
key_facts.excerpt: The incident occurred on Thursday, 25 nautical miles (46 km) northeast of Oman's Khasab, UKMTO said... Ukrainian forces also hit the Louise 1 in July with naval drones in the Black Sea

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC Navy said on Friday two oil tankers were stopped south of Hormuz after ignoring radio warnings and using an 'unauthorized route', and Iran said it destroyed a US unmanned vessel in the eastern strait, with no immediate US confirmation.
key_facts.excerpt: two oil tankers were involved in incidents and stopped in waters south of the Strait of Hormuz, after ignoring radio warnings and attempting to use what it described as an unauthorized route... Iran also said on Friday that it destroyed a US unmanned vessel

key_facts.fact: Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO on Friday that the Iran war is 'going to get wrapped up soon' and that the US needs 'a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon'.
key_facts.excerpt: "It's going to get wrapped up soon," Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO. "We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon," he added.

key_facts.fact: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday in talks coordinated with Washington; Washington wants nuclear issues included from the start while Tehran demands the US first end its port blockade and lift oil export sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday as part of efforts to reach a deal between the US and Iran... Washington wants nuclear issues included from the start of negotiations. Tehran demands that the US first end its port blockade and lift oil export sanctions.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper said US forces had cleared the strait's primary shipping routes of Iranian mines and that more than 50,000 US service members support operations across the Middle East.

key_facts.excerpt: The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, as expected, after raising it by 25 basis points in September... Inflation has climbed to 3.8%, its highest since September 2023, driven by energy prices.

stories.headline: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, says inflation target met for the first time since 2013

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate at 1.25%, the highest since 1995, on Friday, October 30, in an 8-1 vote; board member Hajime Takata dissented in favor of a hike to 1.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: the central bank expectedly held rates at 1.25%, still at its highest level since 1995. The decision was split 8-1, with board member Hajime Takata dissenting. Takata had wanted the bank to hike its policy rate to 1.5%.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ said underlying inflation is 'generally consistent' with its 2% target, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ raised its fiscal 2027 core inflation forecast to 2.6% from 2.4% and said price risks are skewed to the upside; its projections assume Dubai crude falls from about $105 to about $70 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: The BOJ will raise ETF sales to about 860 billion yen a year from January 2027, cutting the time to unwind its holdings to about 43 years from about 112.

stories.headline: Alphabet loses record ~$500B in worst day ever on negative cash flow, dragging Nasdaq 1.4%

key_facts.fact: Alphabet shares fell about 13% on Thursday, October 29, the biggest drop since Google went public in 2004, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market value and passing the previous record decline of 11.63% from March 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet shares plunged the most since Google went public in 2004, dropping 13% on Thursday, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market cap... passing the previous record of 11.63% set in March 2020.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for Q3, versus the $2.7 billion analysts expected, while keeping 2026 capex guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion for the third quarter, compared to the $2.7 billion analysts expected. The Google parent maintained its full year capital expenditure guidance of between $195 billion and $205 billion.

key_facts.fact: Alphabet's market value fell to $3.46 trillion from $3.97 trillion the day before, after it said its AI Mode was eating into search ad revenue.

stories.headline: Israel's final count: Netanyahu bloc wins 53 seats, loses majority; Arab parties take record 19

key_facts.fact: Israel's Central Elections Committee completed the count of Tuesday's election on Thursday: Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 Knesset seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, and Arab-led parties 19, so no camp reached the 61 needed to govern.
key_facts.excerpt: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc won 53 seats in Israel's 120-member Knesset... The bloc supporting Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, won 48 seats... neither secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu's bloc fell well below the 68 seats it controlled at its peak in the previous parliament.
key_facts.excerpt: well below the 68 it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament

key_facts.fact: Likud won 27 seats and Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party 21; the Arab parties' 19 seats nearly double their previous total.
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party won 27, followed by 21 seats for the opposition's centrist Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Two other Arab parties... winning a total of 19 seats. That figure is nearly double the number they had before the election.

key_facts.fact: More than 5.7 million people voted; 306,679 votes went to parties that failed to cross the electoral threshold.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 5.7 million people voted, and 25,789 ballots were disqualified. Another 306,679 votes went to parties that failed to cross the electoral threshold

key_facts.fact: Results will be certified and submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, who will then choose a candidate to try to form a government; Netanyahu remains in charge meanwhile.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's final election results confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations... lie ahead... Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, remains in charge.
